macro_actions.name: Establish Therapeutic Alliance
macro_actions.description: Build rapport, trust, and a collaborative partnership to underpin all therapy phases.

goal.objective: Form a secure, empathetic, and collaborative foundation for therapeutic work.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels understood, trusts the therapist, and is actively engaged in session.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient expresses moderate trust and engagement, but relationship feels tentative.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels disconnected, mistrustful, or unengaged, impeding therapy progress.

goal.reward_hint: Patient actively participates, communicates openly, and expresses feeling understood.

states: Initial contact and early sessions
Patient expresses hesitancy or mistrust
Therapeutic relationship strains emerge
Throughout all sessions for maintenance

macro_actions.name: Conduct Cognitive Case Conceptualization
macro_actions.description: Formulate and collaboratively refine an individualized cognitive conceptualization of the patient’s problems.

goal.objective: Achieve a shared cognitive understanding of the patient’s issues to guide treatment.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient have a clear, agreed-upon cognitive case formulation that guides interventions.
success_levels.acceptable: Case conceptualization is mostly clear but may need refinement; both parties broadly agree.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Case conceptualization is unclear, therapist and patient have differing understandings.

goal.reward_hint: Patient can articulate the cognitive model of their problems and connects it to treatment.

states: Assessment/early sessions
Presentation of complex or poorly understood problems
Need to target interventions to specific cognitions or beliefs
Periods requiring revision of treatment approach

macro_actions.name: Psychoeducation and Socialization to Therapy
macro_actions.description: Educate the patient about the cognitive model, therapy structure, session format, and expectations.

goal.objective: Enable patient understanding of CBT principles, methods, and session norms.

success_levels.ideal: Patient understands key CBT concepts and participates actively according to session structure.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient shows basic comprehension but occasional confusion about therapy methods.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unclear about CBT rationale, leading to disengagement or misunderstanding.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates understanding and adherence to session routines and therapeutic rationale.

states: Early sessions and initial onboarding
When patient queries about therapy process
If patient shows confusion about session structure
When introducing new techniques

macro_actions.name: Collaborative Agenda Setting and Goal Planning
macro_actions.description: Set session agendas and treatment goals in partnership with the patient.

goal.objective: Establish shared, clear session goals and therapeutic objectives.

success_levels.ideal: Patient and therapist collaboratively set and agree upon clear, attainable session and treatment goals.
success_levels.acceptable: Goals are broadly discussed, but some ambiguity or lack of collaboration exists.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Goals are imposed, unclear, or not discussed; patient feels uninvolved.

goal.reward_hint: Patient takes an active role in selecting agenda items and verbalizes goals/goals prioritization.

states: Beginning of every session
Patient requests to address specific topics
Reassessment of treatment objectives needed

macro_actions.name: Assessment and Mood Check
macro_actions.description: Gather mood ratings and biopsychosocial information to inform session focus and priorities.

goal.objective: Acquire current emotional and psychological state to guide intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Accurate information obtained and used to tailor session; patient feels heard.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial assessment completed but may lack depth or specificity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Mood and psychological status not assessed, risking inappropriate focus.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist conducts structured check-in and patient reports mood/emotional state openly.

states: Start of each session
When patient seems emotionally distressed or withdrawn
When shift in mood is observed between sessions

macro_actions.name: Identification and Evaluation of Automatic Thoughts
macro_actions.description: Guide patient to identify, specify, and assess the validity and impact of automatic thoughts.

goal.objective: Patient reliably identifies automatic thoughts and evaluates their accuracy and effects.

success_levels.ideal: Patient regularly and accurately identifies and evaluates automatic thoughts during and between sessions.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient can identify some thoughts but struggles with regularity or specificity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient unable or unwilling to identify or evaluate automatic thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates automatic thoughts and actively participates in thought evaluation tasks.

states: In sessions focused on cognitive restructuring
When patient reports strong emotions or problematic situations
During homework review
When new thought patterns emerge

macro_actions.name: Modification of Intermediate and Core Beliefs
macro_actions.description: Identify, evaluate, and collaboratively modify dysfunctional intermediate and core beliefs.

goal.objective: Reduce the influence of maladaptive core beliefs and strengthen adaptive beliefs.

success_levels.ideal: Patient successfully modifies central negative beliefs and adopts adaptive alternatives.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial modification or awareness of core beliefs; progress is evident but incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Core beliefs remain unaddressed, unchanged, or worsen.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses new perspectives, beliefs, or shows behavioral change based on shifts in core beliefs.

states: After automatic thoughts have been identified and persist
When repeated patterns emerge
If distress or dysfunction seems rooted in deep-seated beliefs
Later therapy stages targeting underlying schemas

macro_actions.name: Skill Acquisition and Behavioral Activation
macro_actions.description: Teach practical coping skills, schedule activities, and plan behavioral experiments to improve functioning.

goal.objective: Equip patient with behavioral and cognitive skills to manage symptoms.

success_levels.ideal: Patient applies targeted coping strategies and behavioral activation techniques with steady improvement.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient tries skills/activities but uses them inconsistently.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient resists skills training or avoids behavioral activation.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes behavioral tasks, demonstrates skill use, and reports improvement in mood/functioning.

states: Sessions focusing on overcoming inactivity or avoidance
When patient struggles with specific behavioral targets
When cognitive interventions alone are insufficient

macro_actions.name: Structured Problem Solving
macro_actions.description: Facilitate analysis, brainstorming, and implementation of solutions to current problems.

goal.objective: Enable patient to resolve present difficulties using a collaborative stepwise approach.

success_levels.ideal: Patient learns and applies structured problem solving independently and effectively.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient engages in some steps, but problem-solving process is incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains stuck or unable/unwilling to engage in structured problem solving.

goal.reward_hint: Patient actively generates solutions, evaluates options, and follows up on plan.

states: When session agenda involves resolving acute problems
Patient reports feeling overwhelmed, stuck, or indecisive
Known barriers identified during therapy

macro_actions.name: Homework Assignment and Review
macro_actions.description: Set, adapt, and review homework assignments collaboratively to promote skill generalization and progress between sessions.

goal.objective: Foster patient autonomy and mastery by practicing skills outside of sessions.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes homework consistently, reports insights, and skill gains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient completes some homework, shows partial engagement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient disengages from homework or fails to complete assignments.

goal.reward_hint: Patient brings completed work, discusses difficulties or successes, and requests new tasks.

states: End of session as ongoing practice
When consolidation of session learning is needed
To address skills acquisition failures
As a tool for relapse prevention

macro_actions.name: Session Summarization and Feedback Elicitation
macro_actions.description: Summarize session key points and elicit patient feedback to reinforce learning and strengthen therapeutic engagement.

goal.objective: Ensure patient comprehension of session content and foster collaborative evaluation.

success_levels.ideal: Patient summarizes learnings and provides constructive feedback.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient acknowledges summary and provides minimal feedback.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Session ends without summary or feedback, patient is confused or uncertain.

goal.reward_hint: Patient restates session takeaways and expresses satisfaction or clarifies misunderstandings.

states: End of each session
If confusion or miscommunication arises
When patient appears disengaged or needs encouragement

macro_actions.name: Termination Preparation and Relapse Prevention
macro_actions.description: Prepare patient for therapy ending, teach relapse prevention strategies, review skills, and ensure maintenance of gains.

goal.objective: Equip patient for lasting self-management, resilience to setbacks, and successful transfer of skills beyond therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels prepared for ending therapy, has clear relapse prevention plan, and maintains gains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient feels somewhat prepared; relapse plan and skills review are incomplete.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels unprepared or anxious, lacking necessary skills/support for termination.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes readiness for termination and demonstrates relapse prevention strategies.

states: Final phase of therapy
During session frequency reduction
When discussing end-of-treatment or setbacks
